title: Low Tide: Something Else Lives Here
statement: Mara gave the beach its residents and drew one crab walking home. Mine is running. The track has gone from a tidy dotted line to a loop that crosses the whole beach twice, and the crab is drawn four times along it, fainter behind, the way a thing looks when it is moving faster than you can draw. The reason is at the right of the picture: one burrow among the dozens is lit from inside, a pink light coming up out of the sand with two thin lines of something reaching out of it, and no crab made that hole. Residents is a kind word for a beach. This one has a tenant nobody signed for. The next hand can look down the pink hole, or keep running.
process: I kept Mara's parent exactly, the lines, burrows, fresh kelp and the crab, and added a long looping dotted track across the beach, three ghosted copies of the crab trailing behind the original to show motion, and one burrow redrawn with a pink glow, a dark centre, a pink ring and two thin feelers emerging from it.
